title: Get the stones out of a running shoe: tip it opening-down with the toe up, shake all 8 out, set it back down
instruction: There are some small stones in this shoe. Get them all out, then put the shoe back down on the table, sole down.
context: Most people have stopped on a walk or a run to take off a shoe and tip out a stone; left in, it rubs a blister (Advnture, 2023). About 52.3 million Americans ran on roads and 17.2 million on trails in 2025, the core of them 50 or more times a year (Outdoor Industry Association, 2026), and about 2.1 billion pairs of footwear were bought in the US in 2024 (World Footwear Yearbook 2025). Everyone does it the same way: hold it by the heel, turn it opening-down with the toe up, shake, put it down. Here a men's US 9 road running shoe at full size (297 g) holds eight gravel pebbles of 4 to 8 mm. The insole slopes down to the toe (10 mm drop), so most stones lie in the toe box under the closed upper, 22 cm or more from the heel, where the opening is. Turned over with the toe still low, they stay there; they leave only when the toe is raised above the opening and the shoe is shaken, and the last one or two catch at the heel and need another shake with the opening straight down.
setup: Centimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top. (1) One men's US 9 road running shoe at true size, modelled on the Nike Pegasus 41 (nike.com/t/pegasus-41-mens-road-running-shoes-LMhfRGdO): 297 g, 10 mm heel-to-toe drop, 37/27 mm stack, outer length 290 mm, widest 100 mm at the ball, collar opening about 100 x 67 mm (length, width and opening are estimates). Blue upper, white midsole, black outsole, white laces; the upper, tongue and laces are one rigid shell with 4.5 mm walls (the real mesh upper is about 1 to 2 mm, an estimate; thinner walls let 4 mm stones tunnel at 240 Hz), closed over the toe box, with a heel counter, a solid 12 mm thick wall standing 120 mm at the back (estimate; the real one is foam-padded and softer); the hand pinches that counter wall, no tab or loop is used. It stands on its sole, laces tied, heel counter at (33, -8), heading 60 degrees from x toward the robot's left (toe at about (47, 17)), opening up. (2) Inside it, 8 gravel pebbles, irregular, 4.1 to 8.0 mm long, 0.04 to 0.28 g (quartz-like, 2.65 g/cm3): 4 in the toe box under the vamp, 2 at the midfoot, 2 at the heel, resting on the insole, which slopes down from the heel to the toe. Nothing else is on the table. Before a real trial, check the pinch: close the gripper pads on a hand-held force gauge until the gripper's motor effort reads 30 to 40 N a finger, then pinch the heel counter at that effort and confirm it lifts the shoe without slipping. Real trial: the Nike Pegasus 41 in US 9 and 8 stones sieved from washed pea gravel between 4 and 8 mm sieves, set on the insole through the collar with tweezers (4 in the toe box, 2 at the midfoot, 2 at the heel).
scoring: Scored at the end, by count and by the shoe's pose. A stone is out when it is no longer in the shoe: not within the shoe's outline above its sole (a stone on the collar's lip counts as in; one on the table under the sole's edge as out). 0.25: at least 2 of the 8 out. 0.5: at least 4 out. 0.75: at least 6 out, or all 8 out but the shoe not set down. 1.0: all 8 out and the shoe set down: resting on its sole on the table (insole within 20 degrees of level), both grippers open and every part of both grippers at least 3 cm from the shoe, all held for the last 2 s. Score 0 if the shoe is dropped or thrown (once a gripper has held it, it is free of both grippers with any point of its sole edge, at heel, toe or either side, more than 1.5 cm above the table (let go in the air, or tipped over after release); or it moves faster than 0.54 m/s, a 1.5 cm fall, while not pinched) or ends off the table. Pinched means both fingertips of one gripper within 3 mm of the shoe and moving with it, each slipping less than 0.1 m/s over the shoe's surface; a finger that merely sits in the collar does not hold it. For the first rule, the highest sole-edge point at the last pinched step counts. Picking a stone out with a finger is allowed and counts. Real trial: count the stones on the table, then tip the shoe into a hand to confirm none is left; level checked against a 20 degree card wedge; the hand's clearance and any drop seen in two phone videos (30 fps or more, at table height, one side-on and one facing the toe, a 1.5 cm tape mark beside the shoe: a release with any edge of the sole, heel, toe or either side, above the mark voids).
reset_notes: Nothing is random: the shoe and the eight stones start at their marks.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at 240 Hz on GPU, CCD on each body and the scene. The shoe is one rigid body (upper, tongue, laces fused): 141 convex pieces, true size, 297 g. Walls 4.5 mm rigid and a solid 12 mm heel counter stand in for the real 1 to 2 mm flexible mesh and foam collar (estimates; thinner walls let 4 mm stones tunnel). Pebbles: irregular convex hulls 4 to 8 mm, 2.65 g/cm3. Estimates: length, collar, counter height, friction 0.5 to 0.6, no restitution.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (682 steps). Lazy routes, all 0: nothing; shaken opening up; opening down with toe low; let go 10, 3 or 2.5 cm up, toe first (narrow or wide grip), re-lifted 3 cm, or hooked by fingers spread in the collar and lifted 5 cm (void); rolled on its side.
